details: Owner, 27 Oct: "Что контролирует целостность и валидность настроек и окружения, точно ли relay doctor сейчас покрывает все или для этого есть прочие утилиты". A scout read of the code that day (verified by the front): every reader of .claude/kit.toml parses its own section ad hoc, and nothing checks keys or values. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen): a typo can switch a guard off.
Also: plugins/delegate/hooks/route-guard.py:150-156 values
Also: plugins/observe/hooks/ledger.py:47 only log_prompts
Also: lib/relay_config.py
Also: lib/relay_setup.py:1066-1180 doctor
failing_case: A project with [delegate] build_tier_opus = "denny" in .claude/kit.toml: a worker started with model opus and no Escalated line is allowed, and relay doctor says nothing.
pass_cases: build_tier_opus = "deny" still denies; the default (no key) still escalates only with an Escalated line
a kit.toml with a syntax error: the route guard names the file and the error; relay doctor reports it
typed_only = "false" (string) is reported as a wrong type, not read as true
an unknown key in [observe] is reported by relay doctor
reason: tests/test_kit_schema.py::test_wrong_type_names_key_and_uses_the_strict_default; the test file fails on the base commit.

details: CONFIRMED by live probes of relay_kit.parse. The design (5.1) says the schema lists every key relay reads and test 11
was to prove it; test 11 was not written and the schema was typed by hand. Case 1 is the worst: with the gate refusing
any problem (owner decision a), a project that sets a documented reminder setting can no longer land a change.
Cases 2 and 3 make doctor say a wrong thing (green on a value relay sync refuses; "used 8" when 0 is used).
Size: 15 minutes (three schema lines plus one cross-check test).
evidence: ['.claude/kit.toml [front] ask_reminder_days is not a key relay knows', '.claude/kit.toml [front] ask_reminder_lines is not a key relay knows']
lib/relay_lane_features.py:14 "out of bounds or not a whole number: the default ... (clamping would turn a 3 and 3 into all features)"
failing_case: 1. kit.toml `[front]\nask_reminder_days = 10\nask_reminder_lines = 3` (both documented in plugins/front/hooks/ask_waiting.py:6-8 and read
there, tested in tests/test_queue_notes.py:495): relay_kit reports "[front] ask_reminder_days is not a key relay knows" and
"[front] ask_reminder_lines is not a key relay knows"; doctor shows two red lines and `relay gate` refuses the branch.
Should: no problem (both keys valid; 1..30 and 1..20 clamped, as the hook does).
2. `[rules]\nwave_min = 9`: relay_kit reports nothing (bounds 1..1000), doctor says "keys and values valid" and the gate passes,
but relay_rules.wave_min_of (lib/relay_rules.py:127-131) refuses anything above 6 and `relay sync` fails.
Should: a problem "[rules] wave_min = 9 is outside 1..6".
3. `[front]\nfeature_lanes = 12`: relay_kit says "is outside 0..8; used 8" (outside="clamp"), but the reader
lib/relay_lane_features.py:13-25 uses 0 for an out-of-bounds value ("clamping would turn a 3 and 3 into all features").
Should: "used 0", the reader's actual value.
fix_hint: Add ask_reminder_days Field("int", 7, bounds=(1, 30), outside="clamp") and ask_reminder_lines Field("int", 5, bounds=(1, 20),
outside="clamp") to [front]; wave_min bounds (1, 6); feature_lanes outside="default". Better: derive the bounds from the
readers' tables (or make the readers import them from relay_kit) and add the cross-check test.
pass_cases:
- parse('[front]
ask_reminder_days = 10
ask_reminder_lines = 3
').problems == ()
- parse('[front]\nask_reminder_days = "x"\n') has one problem naming [front] ask_reminder_days
- parse('[rules]\nwave_min = 9\n') has one problem naming [rules] wave_min; wave_min = 6 has none
- parse('[front]\nfeature_lanes = 12\n') problem line ends "used 0"; feature_lanes = 3 has no problem
- a test that compares the schema with the readers' own tables (relay_lanes.SETTINGS, relay_land.SETTINGS,
relay_metrics.SETTINGS, ask_waiting.DAYS/LINES, relay_rules.LANES_MAX/WAVE_MIN_MAX): every key present, same bounds
(this is design test 11's intent: "fails if the schema lists every key relay reads is false")
findings.summary: the schema disagrees with the code that reads the keys: two documented [front] keys are called unknown (the gate refuses them), wave_min and feature_lanes have the wrong bounds

details: CONFIRMED by reading. The brief: "One typed record and one checking parser ... used by every reader (hooks included) ...
a hook given a broken file says so instead of silently using defaults." The design's table 5.2 lists spec-rule,
flow-stage, lanes and ask_waiting with the note each must give; the worker's report lists them under "Left (not done)".
Only route-guard, ledger and budget were moved. A typo in [specs] method turns a whole workflow off with no word, which
is exactly the class of problem the item exists to end. Project rule (Python): "A record that several programs read
has one typed record and one parser, shared by all of them."
Size: 45 minutes (four hooks, relay_kit links already exist; tests 22-24).
evidence: git diff --stat master...HEAD: no change to plugins/openspec/hooks/spec-rule.py, plugins/relay/hooks/flow-stage.py,
spec-rule.py:44-47: with open(... "kit.toml") ... except Exception: return "none"
flow-stage.py:37-41: with open(... "kit.toml") ... except Exception: return []
worker report: "Left (not done): spec-rule, flow-stage, lanes/ask_waiting hooks ... tests 22-25 not written."
failing_case: kit.toml `[specs]\nmethod = "opnspec"` (a typo): spec-rule.py project_method (lines 41-48) returns "opnspec", no manifest
matches, the hook prints nothing at SessionStart; the OpenSpec rule and steps silently stay off. The same file with
a syntax error: spec-rule.py and flow-stage.py (bindings, lines 36-41) catch every exception and return "none" / [],
the very `except Exception` pattern the item names. Should (design 5.2, test 22): the SessionStart context names
".claude/kit.toml [specs] method" and "opnspec", exit 0.
fix_hint: Each hook takes relay_kit.load(project_root) and puts kit.problems_of(<its section>) into the additionalContext it
pass_cases: - [specs] method = "opnspec", SessionStart: stdout context names ".claude/kit.toml [specs] method" and "opnspec"; exit 0 (design test 22)
- [specs] method = "openspec": today's rule text and steps, no settings note
- no [specs]: spec-rule prints nothing, as today
- [flow] kind = "jria" (a value no plugin binds), UserPromptSubmit: flow-stage context names "[flow] kind" (design test 23)
- [front] feature_lanes = "3": the lanes line uses 0 and names ".claude/kit.toml [front] feature_lanes" (design test 24)
reason: tests/test_openspec_hook.py, test_hook_flow_stage.py, test_lanes_state.py, test_queue_notes.py new cases pass; fail on base.
findings.summary: four hooks still parse kit.toml on their own and say nothing about a wrong value: spec-rule, flow-stage, lanes, ask_waiting

details: CONFIRMED by reading and grep. Design decision 4 (held after review finding F2 of the design review, "the dict API stays,
so most readers bypass the typed record") says load_bindings, get, relay_defaults and every setting()/SETTINGS go and
every reader takes the Kit. Only relay_defaults went. 16 call sites still read the raw dict, and each module keeps its
own bounds table, which is how F1's mismatches arose. Project rule (Python): "A record that several programs read
(a queue item, a verdict) has one typed record and one parser, shared by all of them." Kit.values typed as
dict[str, dict[str, Any]] is not the typed record the rule and design 5.1 ask for.
Size: 120 minutes (the design's estimate for this part; touches lib/relay_land.py, which another lane also changes).
evidence: git grep -n "load_bindings\|relay_config.get(" -- lib plugins bin  -> relay_coverage.py:21,23,84; relay_land.py:41,281;
relay_lane_features.py:17; relay_lanes.py:89,100; relay_metrics.py:65,71,297; relay_rules.py:64; ask_waiting.py:30,40; lanes.py:139
git grep -n "relay_kit.warn\|\.warn(" -- lib plugins bin -> only its definition (lib/relay_kit.py)
failing_case: kit.toml `[land]\nland_tries = 9`: `relay land` reads it through relay_config.load_bindings + relay_land.setting, clamps to 3
and prints nothing; relay_kit's problem for the same line is never shown by the command (design 5.2: "relay_kit.warn on
stderr, once per run"; test 25). relay_kit.warn is defined and called by no code. Also the values relay_kit computes
are a dict[str, dict[str, Any]], not one typed record per section (design 5.1).
Should: `relay land` prints one line ".claude/kit.toml [land] land_tries = 9 is outside 1..3; used 3" on stderr and
lands with 3 tries; load_bindings, get, and the setting() tables are gone.
fix_hint: Per design 5.1/5.2: readers take relay_kit.load(main) and kit.get(section, key); commands call relay_kit.warn(kit, section);
delete load_bindings/get and the SETTINGS tables (the bounds live in SCHEMA only). If the owner prefers to land the
hook part first, this needs his word, as a queue item, not a silent deferral.
pass_cases: - [land] land_tries = 9: relay land uses 3 tries and prints one problem line on stderr (design test 25)
- [land] land_tries = 2: no line, 2 tries
- git grep -n "load_bindings\|relay_config.get(" -- lib plugins bin: no hits outside relay_kit (design decision 4)
- relay_kit.warn has at least one caller, and a second call in the same process prints nothing new
reason: tests/test_land.py and tests/test_kit_schema.py:128 (no second parser) pass; relay_config.load_bindings/get no longer referenced.
findings.summary: the second parser stays: relay_config.load_bindings/get and the modules' setting() still feed land, metrics, coverage, lanes, rules, so their values bypass the checked record (Python rule: one typed record and one parser)

details: CONFIRMED by reading tests/test_kit_schema.py:66-74 and relay_gate.run:438-441. Correct today; the decision is unguarded.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: tests/test_kit_schema.py: relay_gate.refuse_bad_settings(root) called directly; no test goes through relay_gate.run
failing_case: Delete line 441 of lib/relay_gate.py (`refuse_bad_settings(worktree)` inside run): test_gate_refuses_a_branch_with_a_settings_problem
still passes, since it calls relay_gate.refuse_bad_settings(root) itself. Should: a test fails, because the gate would
then pass a branch with build_tier_opus = "denny" (owner decision a).
fix_hint: Drive relay_gate.run (or the `relay gate` CLI) on a temp repo with the bad kit.toml and assert the refusal.
pass_cases: - relay_gate.run on a temp git worktree whose kit.toml has build_tier_opus = "denny": raises GateRefused naming build_tier_opus
- the same worktree with build_tier_opus = "deny": the refusal does not come from settings
findings.summary: the gate test calls refuse_bad_settings directly: removing its call from relay_gate.run keeps every test green

details: CONFIRMED by reading: settings() returns relay_kit.delegate_settings, which uses kit.problems_of("delegate") only.
The strict default applies, so no guard is weakened; the person just gets no reason. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: route-guard.py:141-145 metrics_on reads relay_kit.load(...).get("metrics", "enabled") and drops the problems
failing_case: kit.toml `[metrics]\nenabled = "false"` (text) in a project with .relay/: an unlabelled delegate:worker is denied with
the label text only; nothing says the setting was read as true. Design 5.2 lists route-guard's sections as
"delegate, metrics". Should: the deny reason carries "Settings note: .claude/kit.toml [metrics] enabled ...".
pass_cases: - [metrics] enabled = "false", .relay/ present, unlabelled delegate:worker: deny, reason names "[metrics] enabled"
- [metrics] enabled = false: the worker is allowed without a label, no note
findings.summary: the route guard acts on [metrics] enabled through relay_kit but never names a [metrics] problem

details: CONFIRMED by probe. No live project on this machine has the line (design 2), so the cost is small today. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence:
relay_kit.parse('[observe]
enabled = true
log_prompts = false
') -> ['.claude/kit.toml [observe] enabled is not a key relay knows']
failing_case: A project set up before this change has `[observe]\nenabled = true` (the old template). After this change its gate refuses
with ".claude/kit.toml [observe] enabled is not a key relay knows", which reads as a typo, and `relay setup` on it leaves the
line in place. Design 5.5 promised: "[observe] enabled has no effect: no code reads it; remove the line".
fix_hint: A small table of retired keys with their own sentence, checked before the unknown-key branch in parse.
pass_cases: - parse('[observe]\nenabled = true\n') problem line contains "has no effect" and "remove the line"
- parse('[observe]\nenabld = true\n') still says "is not a key relay knows"
- relay setup on a project whose kit.toml has [observe] enabled = true removes that line (or doctor's red line says to)
reason: tests/test_kit_schema.py:19; setup removal of old line not done, doctor says remove it (acceptable, LOW).
findings.summary: [observe] enabled gets the generic 'is not a key relay knows', not the promised 'has no effect, remove the line', and relay setup does not remove it from older projects whose gate it now refuses
